claims.claim: A blocked virtual thread parks cheaply, so 10k waiting requests become a modest memory footprint.
claims.about: Java 21 virtual threads on Spring Boot (java-spring-vt)
claims.measured: I/O-wait test at 256 connections: java-spring-vt 444 MB peak vs java-spring 491 MB peak (131 MB idle)
claims.why: The benchmark only goes up to 256 concurrent connections, so it can't show memory use at 10,000 parked requests, though at 256 the virtual-thread build already peaked at 444 MB.

claims.claim: With one platform thread per waiting request, 10,000 threads is a poor fit for a container: heavy scheduler overhead, memory pressure.
claims.about: Spring Boot / Tomcat with platform threads (java-spring)
claims.measured: I/O-wait test at 256 connections: java-spring 15,611 req/s, 95% CPU, 491 MB peak
claims.why: No test ran anywhere near 10,000 concurrent connections, so scheduler and memory behaviour at that scale wasn't measured.

claims.claim: Waiting on a payment confirmation costs almost no CPU; what's needed is cheap parking of 10k requests.
claims.measured: I/O-wait test: java-spring 95% CPU and java-spring-vt 75% CPU, but at about 15,000 req/s rather than a few hundred
claims.why: The benchmark measured CPU only at saturation throughput, not at a few hundred completions per second with 10k idle waiters.

claims.claim: Spring WebFlux / Netty, or Vert.x handles this load well.
claims.why: None of these stacks were benchmarked.

claims.claim: The goroutine and async models (Go, Rust, Node, Kotlin coroutines) suit this workload, but the evidence doesn't justify switching away from the JVM.
claims.about: go-gin / go-nethttp, rust-actix / rust-axum, node-fastify / node-express, kotlin-ktor vs java-spring / java-spring-vt
claims.measured: I/O wait, 256 conns: go-gin 20,235, rust-axum 21,042, rust-actix 20,772, kotlin-ktor 21,766, node-fastify 17,462, node-express 14,188 vs java-spring 15,611 and java-spring-vt 14,571 req/s
claims.why: The async stacks do well on the I/O-wait test, and the Java servers are within about 1.5x of them, so the claim that a language switch isn't clearly justified on performance fits the data.

claims.claim: Staying on Java 21 / Spring Boot with virtual threads is enough to handle up to 10,000 concurrent waiting requests (no different language needed).
claims.measured: I/O wait, 256 conns: java-spring-vt 14,571 req/s, p99 37.37 ms, 444 MB peak; no different from java-spring's 15,611 req/s
claims.why: The measured throughput is far above a few hundred completions per second, but nothing was tested at 10,000 concurrent connections, and virtual threads showed no gain over platform threads at 256.
